title: Haydn and the Symphony
objective: After this level you can explain what a symphony is and why Haydn is called its father.
summary: A Classical symphony has four movements: fast, slow, minuet, fast. It grew from the opera overture. Haydn, isolated at Esterháza, wrote over 100 symphonies and is called the Father of the Symphony.

cards.headline: Haydn asked his boss for a holiday without saying a word.
cards.body: In 1772, the Esterházy prince kept his musicians at his summer palace long after they wanted to go home to their families. Haydn answered with a symphony whose finale falls apart on purpose: player after player stops, blows out his candle and walks off. The prince took the hint and let them go. What is a symphony, that it could carry a message like that?

cards.headline: A symphony: four movements for orchestra
cards.body: A symphony is a long work for orchestra in several movements. The typical Classical symphony has four: a fast opening movement, a slow movement, a minuet, and a fast finale. It grew out of the Italian opera overture, the fast-slow-fast sinfonia played before an opera began. So the symphony is, at its root, an opera's curtain-raiser that left the theater and got bigger.

cards.headline: The minuet: a dance in the middle
cards.body: That third movement came from the ballroom. The minuet was an elegant couple dance in moderate triple time, such as 3/4, and it was typically the third movement of a Classical symphony. Count it and you'll hear Level 4's waltz meter: ONE-two-three, ONE-two-three. The symphony stops to dance before its finale.

cards.headline: Stuck in the countryside, forced to be original
cards.body: Joseph Haydn worked for the Esterházy princes for nearly 30 years, starting in 1761. Their palace at Eszterháza was remote. Haydn later said that, cut off from the world with nobody to confuse him, he was "forced to become original." Far from the fashions of the city, he had to find his own way.

cards.headline: Why he's called the Father of the Symphony
cards.body: Haydn didn't invent the symphony; it grew from that opera overture. But he wrote more than 100 of them, which is why he is known as the Father of the Symphony. He had a sense of humor, too. His Surprise Symphony, No. 94, premiered in London in 1792, is named for one startlingly loud chord that crashes into a soft, gentle slow movement.

questions.prompt: In Haydn's Farewell Symphony, what do the players do during the finale?

options.label: All stand up for one loud final chord
options.rationale: The loud chord belongs to the Surprise Symphony.

options.label: Stop one by one, blow out candles, leave
Sing a farewell poem to the prince

questions.explanation: Player after player stops, snuffs his candle and walks off: a hint that the musicians wanted to go home.

questions.prompt: Why is Haydn called the Father of the Symphony if he didn't invent it?

options.label: He wrote the very first symphony
options.rationale: The symphony grew from the Italian opera overture before him.

options.label: He wrote more than 100 and shaped the form
He led the famous Mannheim orchestra
He wrote the first opera overture
options.rationale: Overtures came from Italian opera long before him.

questions.explanation: Symphonies existed before Haydn, but his more than 100 symphonies shaped the form.

questions.prompt: A Classical symphony's minuet shares the meter of Level 4's waltz. How does it count?

options.label: ONE-two, in twos
options.rationale: That is duple meter; the minuet is triple.

options.label: In fives, like a slow march
With no steady beat at all
options.rationale: A dance needs a steady beat.

questions.explanation: The minuet is in moderate triple time, like the waltz's 3/4: ONE-two-three.
